title: With Trump Against Him, Can Ralph Norman Win in South Carolina?
summary: The ultraconservative congressman who has broken with the president on spending is hoping voters reward his experience, contrarian streak and all.

Representative Ralph Norman’s recalcitrant posture may have widened the rift that cleared the way for President Trump’s endorsement of Senator Darline Graham.

By

Reporting from Anderson, Spartanburg and Boiling Springs, S.C.


Aug. 24, 2026


When Representative Ralph Norman addressed about 250 supporters munching on Chick-fil-A chicken nuggets in a civic center in Anderson, S.C., on Friday night, he was quick to acknowledge the biggest obstacle to his bid to become the next Republican senator from South Carolina.


“Who said Donald Trump was the only one who can get a crowd?” Mr. Norman joked, a reference to the thousands of people who had gathered clear across the state on the South Carolina coast, where Mr. Trump was using the power of his presidency and his considerable political muscle[to boost Senator Darline Graham](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/21/us/politics/trump-darline-graham-south-carolina.html) for the job the congressman was seeking.


Republicans in the state will vote on Tuesday in a special runoff election to replace former Senator Lindsey Graham, Ms. Graham’s brother who died last month, on the ballot in November. And Mr. Norman, a hard-line conservative who has staunchly backed Mr. Trump’s agenda over his nine years in Congress but sometimes clashed with him on spending, is hoping that voters will reward his record — contrarian streak and all — and reject the president’s efforts to anoint a senator.


“I mean, the president, he’s an asset wherever he goes — he draws a great crowd,” Mr. Norman said in an interview. “Would I have liked his endorsement? Yeah, I would. But we didn’t, and that’s fine. The people in South Carolina are going to pick their next senator, though.”


Image


A rally for Mr. Norman in Anderson, S.C., on Friday. “Would I have liked his endorsement? Yeah, I would,” Mr. Norman said of the president. “But we didn’t, and that’s fine. The people in South Carolina are going to pick their next senator, though.”


Credit...


Will Crooks for The New York Times


In the critical final days of the abbreviated race, Mr. Norman has found reasons to believe it may be him. There are[signs that Mr. Trump is no longer the Republican kingmaker he once was](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/19/us/politics/trump-primary-election-republican-endorsements.html) , including in South Carolina, where voters[rejected his preferred candidate](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/us/south-carolina-governor-alan-wilson.html) in the governor’s race. Mr. Norman, who ran unsuccessfully in that election, is hoping that voters spurn Ms. Graham — whose[flub at a televised debate last week](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/us/politics/darline-graham-debate-south-carolina.html) highlighted her inexperience — in favor of someone more seasoned.
